name: Scout Ventures
identity_check: Confirmed as Scout Ventures (scout.vc; also styles itself Scout VC), the dual-use / national-security seed fund founded by West Point graduate Brad Harrison. Its management company is Scout VC, LLC. SEC Form Ds for Scout Ventures Fund III, IV, V, V-A and the Fund V - VA Sidecar all name Bradley C. Harrison as manager of the GP. Fund IV and V filings use 2903 Oak Haven Drive, Austin TX; Fund III (2017-18) used 63/65 North Moore St, New York. Formerly BHV (Brad Harrison Ventures), New York, renamed Scout Ventures in August 2013 (PE Hub). The Fund III GP is 'BHV Entrepreneurship Fund III GP, LLC', and BHV Entrepreneurship Fund IA shares Scout's 917-656-5665 phone, so the BHV Entrepreneurship Fund vehicles (2011-2015) are this firm's earlier funds. Not Sequoia Capital's scout fund (fund-list row 'Sequoia Ventues - Scout Fund', $180M, 2018, Bay Area). Not LiveOak Venture Partners (Austin), whose fund article the list's 2013 'Scout Ventures' row links to. An EDGAR company search for 'scout venture' returns only the five Scout Ventures Fund entities above.

thesis_text.value: Seed-stage dual-use VC backing founders from the military, intelligence community and national labs. Leads seed rounds and reserves for follow-ons through Series B, focusing on AI, autonomy and robotics, space, cybersecurity, quantum, microelectronics, advanced materials and advanced power; Fund V adds critical minerals, advanced manufacturing and simulation. Helps portfolio companies win non-dilutive government funding; avoids weapons/kinetic plays.

open_items: Fund V Business Wire release (businesswire.com/news/home/20260310158864) returned 403 to both fetchers. Fund V close date and size rest on Tectonic Defense, the scout.vc media listing and the Form D offering amount.

Final sizes and close dates for BHV Entrepreneurship Fund LP (Fund I), Fund IA and Fund II were not found. The Form Ds give only offering amounts, and Fund II's amendments report $0 sold despite 24-30 investors.
invests_in_indian_founders: not stated on any page read. Portfolio is US-centred, with one UK company (Valarian).
requires_us_entity: not stated. The 2026 boilerplate stresses U.S. national security, but no entity rule was found.
No current NYC office could be confirmed. The site lists no addresses and recent filings are all Austin. Ian Folau covers the western US from Utah.
AFR (2015-10-21) reported a planned $40 million Australian fund. No evidence was found that it launched, and the currency (AUD or USD) is unclear.
Former partners Wes Blackwell and Sam Ellis (TechCrunch 2021) and Fund III director Brendan Syron (Form D 2018) are not on the current team page. They are not recorded.
Valarian $7M round: the stage is not stated and the date is approximate (Valarian post dated 09.05.2025). Valarian's later $50M Series A (2026-07-14) does not name Scout.

The shared web-search budget ran out mid-task. Rounds were gathered from scout.vc media links and portfolio company sites. No Scout-named round pages were found on the sites of Aeglos (stealth), Reaxiomatic, Citra Space, Swarmbotics, TernAI, Swan, Sicura, XPonent Power or FluxWorks.
Havoc Series A (2026-05-12) names no lead. Scout ('Scout VC') is listed among existing investors.
